external_entities.name: supplier
external_entities.description: A supplier that uploads compliance paperwork and signs in to the portal.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal — insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for their own staff.

external_entities.name: category manager
external_entities.description: A category manager who reviews uploaded paperwork and approves or rejects it.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.

external_entities.name: vendor
external_entities.description: The vendor that hosts the SaaS portal and pushes the nightly supplier data extract.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The portal is a SaaS product. The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

processes.name: supplier portal
processes.description: A vendor-hosted SaaS portal through which suppliers upload paperwork and category managers review and approve or reject it.
processes.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal

processes.name: supplier master service
processes.description: A service that loads the nightly supplier data extract and writes the records into the supplier database.
processes.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_stores.name: vendor platform
data_stores.description: The vendor platform where supplier compliance documents remain.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

data_stores.name: landing bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket in the organization's cloud account that receives the nightly supplier data extract.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.

data_stores.name: supplier database
data_stores.description: The database into which the supplier master service writes supplier records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_flows.name: upload paperwork
data_flows.description: A supplier uploads compliance paperwork and staff contact details to the supplier portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal — insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for their own staff.
data_flows.data_description: insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for suppliers' own staff

data_flows.name: review paperwork
data_flows.description: A category manager reviews uploaded paperwork and approves or rejects it through the supplier portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.
data_flows.data_description: uploaded compliance paperwork and approval or rejection decisions

data_flows.name: store paperwork
data_flows.description: The supplier portal stores supplier compliance documents in the vendor platform.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

data_flows.name: push data extract
data_flows.description: The vendor pushes a nightly supplier data extract to the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_flows.notes: Encryption disagreement: System description says "We were told the nightly extract is encrypted end to end." The same source also says "The runbook for the landing bucket says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is."

data_flows.name: load extract
data_flows.description: The supplier master service loads the nightly extract from the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file

data_flows.name: write records
data_flows.description: The supplier master service writes the extracted supplier records into the supplier database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the records into the supplier database

trust_boundaries.name: vendor hosting
trust_boundaries.description: The vendor-hosted environment containing the SaaS portal and vendor platform.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which category managers work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organization's cloud account containing the landing bucket, supplier master service, and supplier database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

assumptions.assumption: The compliance paperwork and staff contact details are confidential because they contain personal details and business records.
assumptions.basis: Suppliers present compliance paperwork and contact details for their own staff.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier portal holds confidential data because it handles compliance paperwork and staff contact details.
assumptions.basis: The portal is used to upload compliance paperwork and contact details for suppliers' staff.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier master service holds confidential data because it loads and writes supplier records.
assumptions.basis: The service loads a supplier data extract and writes supplier records.

assumptions.assumption: The vendor platform's contents are confidential because it stores compliance paperwork and staff contact details.
assumptions.basis: The documents remain in the vendor platform and include compliance paperwork and staff contact details.

assumptions.assumption: The landing bucket's contents are confidential because it receives supplier data extracts.
assumptions.basis: The landing bucket receives a supplier data extract containing supplier records.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier database's contents are confidential because it stores supplier records.
assumptions.basis: The supplier master service writes supplier records into the supplier database.
